thread.title: Wildfire evacuation zone grows north of Reno as fires' perimeter goes over 100,000 acres - NewsBreak
thread.title_full: Wildfire evacuation zone grows north of Reno as fires' perimeter goes over 100,000 acres - NewsBreak

author: Greg Haas
title: Wildfire evacuation zone grows north of Reno as fires' perimeter goes over 100,000 acres - NewsBreak
text:
By Greg Haas ,
9 hours ago LAS VEGAS ( KLAS ) — The perimeter of wildfires north of Reno has now grown to 104,488 acres, and containment is improving as more resources arrive to fight the fire.
Going into Wednesday, water scoopers defended houses and structures in the fires’ paths. Evacuation zones now stretch from the California border to areas about 30 miles to the east at the southern tip of Pyramid Lake.
But as Wednesday evening arrived, officials said containment has improved as ground and air crews worked hard to reduce risks to nearby communities.
The Bug Fire and the Fred Mountain Fire have combined, and reports now refer to it as just the Bug Fire. As of Wednesday evening, it was at 70,757 acres, according to the Southwest Area Incident Management Team. The Stallion Fire, east of the Bug Fire, has now burned 33,731 acres.
Reno-area Animal Ark sanctuary among those affected by wildfires Personnel assigned to the fires nearly doubled on Wednesday, growing to 771. Most — 579 — are working against the Bug Fire. Combined, there are seven crews, 25 engines, five helicopters and nine dozers working in the area.
Wildfires continue to burn north of Reno. The combined perimeters of the Bug Fire and the Stallion Fire are now 104,488 acres. (Photo: BLM) Fire managers say the Bug Fire is 3% contained and the Stallion Fire remains at 0% containment.
“Eight large air tankers, two very large air tankers, four water scoopers, and multiple water-dropping helicopters flew in support of ground crews throughout the day, combining with the coordinated defense of communities on all sides of the Bug Fire and along the east side of the Stallion Fire,” a daily update from fire managers said.
“While the containment percentage has decreased, the primary objectives of preventing structure loss and ensuring public safety through coordinated, timely evacuations were achieved,” the update said.
As of 6:45 p.m. on Wednesday, the evacuation zone had expanded significantly to the northeast, almost covering the western edge of Pyramid Lake. An estimated 4,000 people have been displaced by the fires.
Firefighters from the Las Vegas valley were sent to support, covering duties of firefighters in the region who had been dispatched to join the effort against the wildfires.
All three fires were human-caused, and a woman was arrested on an arson charge in connection with the Fred Mountain Fire on Tuesday.
A social media post from the Reno-Sparks Indian Colony told residents of Hungry Valley that the community remains in the evacuation zone. Tribal authorities and the Washoe County Sheriff’s Office are coordinating evacuations. Evacuees are being sent to the Evelyn Mount Community Center at 1013 Valley Road in Reno.
Washoe County continued closures at eight schools on Wednesday, and added a ninth to the list: Natchez Elementary School. The school district had closed these schools earlier this week: Desert Heights Elementary, Silver Lake Elementary, Lemmon Valley Elementary, Alyce Taylor Elementary, Jesse Hall Elementary, Spanish Springs Elementary, Shaw Middle School and and Spanish Springs High School.
Gov. Joe Lombardo declared a state of emergency Monday afternoon. The perimeter of the fires has expanded by more than 500% since then, pushed by winds with gusts up to 30 mph.
>>Download the free 8 News+ app for live newscasts and streaming originals High temperatures and low humidity are persisting. Thunderstorms are forecast Wednesday afternoon and into tomorrow, and officials warned storms could produce stronger, sudden outflow winds from any direction, along with lightning. A flash flood watch is in effect for areas near older burn scars.
